verdict.rationale: Semgrep ships curated security rulesets (e.g. p/python, p/security-audit) and a CLI that scans for classes like injection; a hands-on probe confirms it actually flags a shell-injection pattern (`subprocess-shell-true`) out of the box with no login required, and community reviews corroborate its value for security lint rules (e.g. authorization checks, semantic detection beyond regex). Some community reports note false negatives/bypassable patterns (comm-6, comm-10) and performance concerns, which temper but don't negate the core capability. Missing for 10: independent benchmark specifically for XSS detection, and resolution of the noted simple-bypass false-negative reports.
